items.q: The definition of chronic kidney disease on this page describes the net consequence of a fall in viable nephrons. What intraglomerular hypertension ultimately results in?
items.exp: Definition: net consequence of the ↓ in no. of viable nephrons leading to intraglomerular hypertension resulting in proteinuria. (Book p805)

items.q: Fill up: GFR = viable no. of nephrons × single nephron (sn) ______.
items.exp: Pathogenesis: GFR = viable no. of nephrons × single nephron (sn) GFR. (Book p805)

items.q: Viable nephrons can be regenerated or replaced after birth.
opts: False — they are fixed according to birth weight
items.exp: Viable nephrons: fixed according to birth weight; not regenerated/replaced. (Book p805)

items.q: The number of viable nephrons in a person is fixed according to:
items.exp: Viable nephrons: fixed according to birth weight; not regenerated/replaced. (Book p805)

items.q: Match the following pathogenesis step to its consequence — 1) ↓ no. of nephrons  2) Glomerular hyperfiltration  3) Mechanical stretching … A) Intraglomerular hypertension  B) ↑↑ sn GFR to maintain GFR  C) Capillary, podocyte and mesangial cell injury
items.exp: ↓ no. of nephrons → ↑↑ sn GFR to maintain GFR → glomerular hyperfiltration → intraglomerular hypertension → mechanical stretching of capillary, podocyte and mesangial cell. (Book p805)

items.q: Match the following stretched glomerular cell to its response — 1) Capillary  2) Podocyte  3) Mesangial cell … A) Proliferation → glomerular sclerosis (GS)  B) ↓ nephrin expression via local RAAS activation through AT-II  C) ↑ capillary pore diameter → proteinuria (tubulotoxic)
items.exp: Mechanical stretching: capillary → ↑ capillary pore diameter → proteinuria (tubulotoxic); podocyte → local RAAS activation via AT-II → ↓ nephrin expression; mesangial cell → proliferation → glomerular sclerosis (GS). (Book p805)

items.q: All but one are components of the red-letter mnemonic written beneath the flowchart. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Mnemonic: IF TA GS — interstitial fibrosis, tubular atrophy, glomerular sclerosis. (Book p805)

items.q: Fill up: Tubulotoxic proteinuria triggers interstitial inflammation, which releases ______ to drive interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy.
items.exp: Proteinuria is tubulotoxic → interstitial inflammation releases TGF-β → interstitial fibrosis (IF) + tubular atrophy (TA). (Book p805)

items.q: The tubulointerstitium, the determinant of renal function decline, makes up what share of the kidney?
items.exp: Determinant of renal function decline: tubulointerstitium (85-90% of kidney is tubulointerstitium). (Book p805)

items.q: The tendency to progress independently of etiology sets in after what fraction of nephrons are destroyed?
items.exp: Tendency to progress independent of etiology: after 50% nephrons are destroyed. (Book p805)

items.q: A patient who has one kidney removed at birth retains fewer viable nephrons. To keep total GFR stable, each surviving nephron must:
items.exp: ↓ no. of nephrons → ↑↑ sn GFR to maintain GFR (compensation of surviving nephrons). (Book p805)

items.q: In the flowchart, the podocyte responds to mechanical stretching with local RAAS activation via AT-II.
opts: True, but only after 90% nephron loss
items.exp: Podocyte → local RAAS activation via AT-II → ↓ nephrin expression. (Book p805)

items.q: According to the page, the determinant of renal function decline in CKD is the:
items.exp: Determinant of renal function decline: tubulointerstitium (85-90% of kidney is tubulointerstitium). (Book p805)
